design.front_end: scp4d_fe_w: W-byte beats -> byte queue (2W) -> header bytes one per cycle | payload varint tokens (tokenizer, W bytes/cycle, zigzag pre-decode) -> token queue (2W + K)
design.tdec_w: issue chain of W steps per cycle (one token or one sweep element each), P = W banks of state memory (element e -> bank e mod P), per-bank A/B pipeline as scp4d_tdec
design.rdec_w: scp4d_rdec datapath unchanged; payload consumed as tokens; W >= 2 retires head + first index and q + next gap in one cycle (one event per cycle); W = 4 same as W = 2 on the parser side
design.cycle_model: scripts/scp-v0113-rtl-model.ts: register-transfer cycle model (full-rate input); cycles = cycle of the last frame + 4 (tdec_w) / 5 (rdec_w) drain

verdict.temporal_only: Pays off in cycles, less in wall-clock time. Env T64: 1.9992× fewer cycles at W = 2 and 3.6701× at W = 4 (bank conflicts end 17.03% of W = 4 payload cycles). With ECP5 fmax estimates the best wall-clock point is W2: W = 4's 4-step issue chain roughly halves fmax, so W = 4 is about as fast as W = 2 in time.
verdict.relations: Little: env T64 gets 1.164× at W = 2 and 1.164× at W = 4. 81.21% of W = 2 cycles are fan-out, settle and flush, which do not read the stream (Amdahl limit with an infinitely wide input: 1.4332×).
verdict.new_bottleneck: temporal-only: the combinational issue chain (token select -> step decode -> index add -> bank check, repeated W times, then the token-queue pop) sets fmax, and bank conflicts cap W = 4 at ~3.7× fewer cycles; relations: the one-ACC-update-per-cycle fan-out and the per-frame dirty flush (stream input is no longer the limit).
verdict.relations_vs_temporal: Unchanged, and stronger: inside the decoder relations stay slower at every W (time ratio 2.5815× at W = 2); they only finish first when the link feeding the decoder is slower than ~30.82 MB/s (W = 2, ECP5 estimates; ~29 MB/s in v0.1.12). Keep temporal-only as the hardware default; relations remain a memory/link-bound option.
